references.text: Joshua receives the same command to meditate on the Book of the Law day and night in order to observe and do everything written in it.
The blessed man finds his delight in the Lord's law and meditates on it day and night, reflecting the king's daily reading of the law.
The psalmist expresses love for God's law and meditates on it all day long, corresponding to the king's lifelong commitment to the Book of the Law.
The fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge, which connects to the king's instruction to fear the Lord his God.
Moses commands the people to fear the Lord and keep all His laws and commandments all the days of their lives.
The people are to gather to hear the law, learn to fear the Lord, and observe all the words of the law.
Timothy has known the holy Scriptures from childhood, and all Scripture is useful for teaching, just as the king studies God's word daily.
Blessed is the one who reads aloud the words of this prophecy and those who hear it and keep what is written in it, reflecting the blessing of reading and keeping God's word.
